title: A stranger on my train left a clue. Part 4
note: Silent, stands alone, no recap. Frame 1 = moving carriage, QUIET CARRIAGE sign, her clue 'Look at the (6)' with 6 empty boxes, his hand already closing on his phone (plain lock screen 7:44, no notifications). Take 1 (SCREEN): he looks at the phone, she turns to the window; the train jolts to a halt, the phone slides off the table and he dives after it; she points her pen at the window with a kind nudge (the balloon is never shown in take 1); joke is on him only; the opposite train runs BACKWARDS as the rewind. Take 2 (WINDOW): both flip their phones face down, the same halt arrives gently (his palm stops his phone), a lone orange balloon rises over the hills and they see it together; he writes WINDOW, she answers with a green tick and a balloon doodle. The train rolls, the board flips to NEXT STOP, she stands and writes 'Tomorrow, same (4)', glances back unsure from the door. Vote A SEAT (I'll save her seat) vs B TIME (7:42, same as ever). B wins in part 5. Only the vote uses A and B; tags are takes. All times in seconds.

cast.her: mustard scarf, pen, booklet, small phone under the booklet (face down at 7.9 in take 2); stands from 14.5; blush only in take 2

hooks.a: A stranger on my train left a clue. I missed it.
hooks.b: She wrote me a clue. I checked my phone instead.

clues.text: green tick and a tiny balloon doodle

choices.question: what should I write?
choices.part5: A plays first and fails: next morning he arrives early and parks his coat on her seat, fends off a commuter with a taken nod, and she never appears; he sits guarding an empty seat (joke on him only); rewind (opposite train backwards); B TIME carries on: 7:42, the seat is empty, she isn't on the train; he finds her booklet page with a new clue under the table clip; next vote sets up part 6 Last stop

strips.text: her crossword clue for me. I check my phone.
I looked down. she looked out.
